title: Isotopic Labeling of Cyanobacteria and DNA Analysis
author: Bonnie Poulos
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.c9nz5d
materials: Growth medium (Pro99, SN, SNAX or Amp1)
Extract bacterial DNA using standard methods.
For density gradient centrifugation, a Beckman VTi 65 vertical rotor was used with 13x48 mm OptiSeal polyallomer tubes (4.9 ml capacity).

steps.title: Prepare 15N Labeled Growth Medium
steps.instruction: Prepare Pro99, SN, SNAX or Amp1 medium according to the standard recipe, substituting the normal nitrogen source with 15N‑ammonium chloride (15NH4Cl, 99% 15N, Cambridge Isotope Laboratories, Catalog #NLM-467-1).

steps.title: Grow Cyanobacteria with Heavy Nitrogen
steps.instruction: Inoculate the prepared medium with cyanobacteria and grow under appropriate conditions, performing at least three successive transfers in the 15N medium before experimental use.

steps.title: Harvest Heavy‑Nitrogen Cyanobacteria
steps.instruction: Harvest the cultured cyanobacteria grown in the heavy‑nitrogen medium by standard centrifugation or filtration methods.

steps.title: Extract and Quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA and quantify it using the Quant‑iT™ PicoGreen® dsDNA Assay Kit (Life Technologies, Catalog #P7589) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Confirm Minimum DNA Quantity
steps.instruction: Verify that the DNA yield is ≥10 µg, which is the minimum amount required for the subsequent density‑gradient centrifugation.

steps.title: Configure Density Gradient Centrifuge
steps.instruction: Set up a Beckman VTi 65 vertical rotor with 13 × 48 mm OptiSeal polyallomer tubes (capacity 4.9 ml). Ensure the ultracentrifuge (Beckman L70 or L80) is ready for use.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the DNA in TE buffer (10 mM Tris, 1 mM EDTA, pH 7.6) to a final volume of 0.9 ml.

Add 4 ml of CsCl solution prepared in the same TE buffer, adjusting the CsCl concentration so that the mixture has an initial density of 1.8 g ml⁻¹ (verify that the final solution density is ≈1.7 g ml⁻¹).

steps.title: Load Mixture into OptiSeal Tubes
steps.instruction: Dispense the complete 4.9 ml DNA‑CsCl mixture into an OptiSeal tube and seal it with the black cap; then place the capped tubes into the rotor carriers and secure the carrier caps.

steps.title: Ultracentrifuge Gradient Tubes
steps.instruction: Run the ultracentrifuge at 44,000 rpm (≈184,678.5 g) for 48 h at 18 °C using a Beckman L70 or L80 rotor.

steps.title: Collect Gradient Fractions
steps.instruction: After centrifugation, collect fractions of 0.2–0.25 ml from each tube.

steps.title: Quantify DNA and Measure Fraction Densities
steps.instruction: Determine the DNA concentration in each fraction in duplicate with the Quant‑iT PicoGreen assay and record the density of each fraction.

steps.title: Plot DNA Amount versus CsCl Density
steps.instruction: Plot ng of DNA versus measured CsCl density for the fractions that contain DNA to determine the buoyant density profile.
